caveats: **No documented business driver.** The roadmap verification of 2026-09-19 found zero documented business driver anywhere in the four planning docs for this plugin; it ships as a read-only inventory fact source, not a response to a stated customer requirement.

**Machine scope, default prefixes, point in time.** Per-user package stores are out of scope, deferred to the user-session helper (ADR-3003): per-user Homebrew, npm global-versus-user, pip user installs and cargo are not read. Only the two default Homebrew prefixes are probed: a Homebrew relocated to a custom or symlinked prefix reads as absent (zero rows) or refused (`constrained`), not as installed. Names are read from a live tree, so an entry removed between the listing and its classification is skipped as absent, not reported. A stalled mount inside the tree can pin one agent worker per action until it answers (later dispatches report `busy`), because the walk's deadline is cooperative; recover with a normal agent restart ("Stopping a wedged agent", `docs/user-manual/server-admin.md`).

**Linux `packages` is unsupported by design; manager versions and more manager facts are not read; snap and flatpak specifics.** Linux `managers` reports presence and the apt, snap and flatpak counts only: every version is `-` (a version read would be a subprocess), and the dpkg, rpm, dnf, pacman and apk facts, the flatpak `metadata` read (runtime field, appdata version) and manager versions are deferred to #5851. installed_apps owns the distro-package roster, so Linux `packages` never emits a `package|` row. Snap and flatpak specifics: (a) A snap whose revision is unmounted, unreadable or whose `snap.yaml` is hostile is a row with version `-` and kind `unknown`, silent on the status by design: a constrained answer would stall the whole installed-software cycle for as long as the cause persists, and `snap.yaml` is snap-author-controlled text that only reaches a row through the closed kind token and snapd's version grammar. An absent or unopenable `/snap` mount tree makes every snap `unknown`, so all of them leave the catalogue (like a `snap disable`d snap, (b)) while the rest of the host's roster stays fresh: this is chosen over a constrained answer, which would skip the whole installed-software cycle for as long as the mount tree is broken. The `unknown` state is visible on the wire row only, not in the catalogue. (b) A `snap disable`d snap loses its `current` link, so every revision of it is `inactive` and it leaves the catalogue. (c) The `.Locale` and `.Debug` flatpak extension runtimes are emitted as runtime rows although `flatpak list` hides them. (d) Only the system installation (`/var/lib/flatpak`) and the default snap roots (`/snap`, falling back to `/var/lib/snapd/snap`) are read; per-user flatpak installs are out of scope. (e) A walk blocked in a syscall on a stalled `/snap/<name>/<rev>` mount blocks the sync scheduler's SEQUENTIAL source loop (`src.collect()` runs inline), so `installed_software` and every later daily-sync source wait behind it: the single-flight slot only refuses CONCURRENT dispatches (`linux:<action>:busy`) and the per-entry deadline only bounds the readdir loops, neither cures a hung open. There is no mountinfo guard (the roots are fixed and local, and a dead FUSE daemon answers ENOTCONN rather than hanging). (f) A `linux:managers:busy` answer, or any constrained `managers` answer with zero present rows, skips that sync cycle (a transient single-flight; same posture as macOS). (g) The Linux sample in `docs/samples/linux.txt` comes from a Debian container with no snapd or flatpak (`store_packages` is `supported` with zero rows); the real snap and flatpak rows are proven by the committed capture tree, taken on a WSL2 guest, which does not prove behaviour on a bare-metal or LXD host.

**Homebrew rows overlap `installed_apps` on macOS, and cask and tap rows are unexercised against real data.** Homebrew casks install `.app` bundles that `installed_apps`' macOS `list` also reports via `system_profiler`, and `installed_apps`' `list_per_user` already lists Homebrew formulae per user as `user_app|brew|<name>|<version>|-|-` (it runs `brew list --versions`); this plugin is the machine-scope, zero-subprocess view of the same store (manager identity, prefixes, cask versions) and does not claim to be disjoint from either. The real-capture host had a populated `Cellar` only (no `Library/Taps`, empty `Caskroom`, no `/usr/local` Homebrew), so tap and cask counting and the Intel prefix are covered only by synthetic in-code layouts that encode the layout the walk assumes, not by a real capture. The Intel `Library/Taps` location (`<prefix>/Homebrew/Library/Taps`) is taken from Homebrew's own scripts, not from an Intel capture. Gating differs on purpose: `installed_apps.list_per_user` is admin-or-approval because it attributes packages to users, whereas this machine-scope roster is `Inventory:Read` (ungated), like `installed_apps.list`.

**Windows legs planned — each follows as its own PR.** All three Windows actions report `status|<action>|unsupported|windows:planned` and no data rows. The Chocolatey `lib\` directory walk with `.nuspec` metadata, winget presence and the Appx store roster follow as their own PRs; nothing for them is built here.

definitions.description: Reports the packages installed under a package manager, read from directory names with no subprocess. macOS reports Homebrew formulae (Cellar/<formula>/<version>) and casks (Caskroom/<cask>/<version>) over both /opt/homebrew and /usr/local. A formula or cask present under both prefixes yields one row per prefix. Linux is UNSUPPORTED by design: installed_apps owns the Linux package roster, so this action reports `status|packages|unsupported|linux:owned_by_installed_apps` and no package row. Windows is not implemented in this release and reports `status|packages|unsupported|windows:planned`. Machine scope only: per-user package stores are out of scope, deferred to the user-session helper (ADR-3003). Homebrew casks install .app bundles that installed_apps' macOS `list` also reports via system_profiler, and installed_apps' `list_per_user` lists Homebrew formulae per user, so this action does not claim to be disjoint from either; it adds the manager identity and the cask version.

Reports which package managers are present on the endpoint and their manager-level configuration facts, read from the filesystem with no subprocess. macOS reports each Homebrew prefix found under /opt/homebrew and /usr/local with tap, formula and cask counts. Linux reports which of dpkg, apt, rpm, dnf, pacman, apk, snap and flatpak are present (never a package roster) with apt, snap and flatpak counts as facts. Windows is not implemented in this release and reports `status|managers|unsupported|windows:planned`. Machine scope only: per-user package stores are out of scope, deferred to the user-session helper (ADR-3003). A status row always comes first; a genuinely absent manager produces no manager row, while an unreadable location makes the status row `constrained` with a failure token.

Reports the snaps and flatpak apps and runtimes installed on a Linux endpoint, read from the system stores with no subprocess. Snaps come from /var/lib/snapd/snaps/<name>_<revision>.snap joined to the /snap/<name> mount tree (the `current` link gives the active revision; the mounted revision's meta/snap.yaml gives the version and type). Flatpaks come from /var/lib/flatpak/{app,runtime}/<id>/<arch>/<branch> with the `active` link giving the commit. Flatpak metadata is not read, so a flatpak row has no version. A single snap or flatpak whose metadata cannot be read is still reported, with version `-` and kind `unknown` or state `unknown`, and does not change the status; the status is `constrained` only when the LIST may be incomplete (an unlistable directory, a cap or budget, or a concurrent dispatch). macOS is UNSUPPORTED by design (installed_apps owns the application list) and reports `status|store_packages|unsupported|macos:owned_by_installed_apps`. Windows is not implemented in this release and reports `status|store_packages|unsupported|windows:planned`. Machine scope only.

description: Machine-scope package-manager inventory (managers, packages and store_packages); per-user package stores are out of scope, deferred to the user-session helper
how_it_works: `managers` reports which package managers are present on the host and their manager-level configuration facts; `packages` lists the macOS Homebrew formulae and casks; `store_packages` lists the snaps and flatpak apps and runtimes installed on Linux. All three are pure filesystem reads (`open`/`openat`/`readdir`/`readlinkat`, leaf no-follow with root-owned parents trusted: each directory is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW`, so a symlinked prefix, marker or store directory is refused, never followed, while the OS-owned parents such as `/opt`, `/usr` and `/var` are not checked): no `brew`, `dpkg`, `rpm`, `pacman`, `apk`, `snap`, `flatpak` or `winget` is ever spawned. Every action writes a `status` row first, then data rows. On macOS, both actions probe both Homebrew prefixes (`/opt/homebrew` on Apple silicon, `/usr/local` on Intel): `managers` reads directory names under `Library/Taps` (at `<prefix>/Homebrew/Library/Taps` on current Intel installs, where Homebrew keeps its repository, otherwise `<prefix>/Library/Taps`), `Cellar` and `Caskroom`, and `packages` reads `Cellar` and `Caskroom`. On Linux, `managers` checks for the eight tools (dpkg, apt, rpm, dnf, pacman, apk, snap, flatpak) with a no-follow stat under `/usr/bin`, `/usr/sbin`, `/bin` and `/sbin`, and adds the counts a real capture supports (the apt `*.list`/`*.sources` file count, the snap file count, the flatpak app and runtime counts); `store_packages` joins `/var/lib/snapd/snaps/<name>_<revision>.snap` to the `/snap/<name>` mount tree (the `current` link is read with `readlinkat` and validated as a bare revision, never resolved; one bounded, no-follow read of `<revision>/meta/snap.yaml` gives the version and type) and walks `/var/lib/flatpak/{app,runtime}/<id>/<arch>/<branch>` with the `active` link giving the commit. Linux `packages` is unsupported by design (`installed_apps.list_inventory` owns the Linux package roster). Machine scope only: per-user package stores are out of scope, deferred to the user-session helper (ADR-3003). On Windows all three actions read nothing and report `status|<action>|unsupported|windows:planned` (caveat 5). Every walk takes an injected root (production passes `/`) so the unit suite drives it over a committed fixture tree and through the real emission seam.
name: pkg_inventory

Status rows: the completeness level. Values: supported, constrained (at least one read failed), unsupported (the planned Windows leg).

A key is omitted when its source could not be read completely (unreadable, truncated at the entry cap, or out of walk budget).

columns.description: Manager rows only: failure tokens for an unavailable manager (macOS only; Linux never reports unavailable), or "-".

columns.name: manager

Status rows: the completeness level. Values: supported, constrained (the list may be incomplete), unsupported (macOS by design, Windows planned).

columns.description: Snap rows: the snap.yaml `version`, or "-" when the revision is not mounted or readable or the value is not a plain one-line scalar that passes snapd's version grammar. Flatpak rows: always "-" (the appdata version is not read; the branch is a ref, not a version). Status rows: the comma-joined failure tokens, or "-" when none. Tokens read <os>:<source>:<detail>: linux:snapd_snaps:*, linux:flatpak_app:* and linux:flatpak_runtime:* (an unlistable directory, entry_cap or walk_budget), linux:store_packages:row_cap, linux:store_packages:byte_cap, linux:store_packages:busy, macos:owned_by_installed_apps, windows:planned or pkg_inventory:exception (a leg threw).

columns.description: Package rows only. Snap: the snap.yaml `type` (app is the default when absent; application reads as app), or unknown when snap.yaml could not be read, or other for an unrecognised type. Flatpak: app or runtime. Status rows: "-".
columns.name: kind

columns.description: Package rows only: the snap revision, or the flatpak commit (64 hex digits); "-" when a flatpak branch has no readable `active` link.
columns.name: revision

columns.description: Package rows only: the flatpak architecture (e.g. x86_64); "-" for snaps.
columns.name: arch

columns.description: Package rows only: the flatpak ref branch (e.g. stable, 51, 26.08-extra); "-" for snaps. A branch is a ref, not a version.
columns.name: branch

columns.description: Package rows only: active (the snap `current` link or the flatpak `active` link points at this revision), inactive (present but not current), unknown (the link could not be read). Status rows: "-".
columns.name: state

outputs_note: Pipe-delimited rows written via `write_output()`, two shapes per stream discriminated by field 0: exactly one `status|<action>|<supported\|constrained\|unsupported>|<failure tokens or ->` row first, then zero or more data rows — `manager|<name>|<present\|unavailable>|<version or ->|<root_path or ->|<facts k=v;... or ->|<reason or ->` for `managers`, `package|homebrew|<id>|<version>|<formula\|cask>` for `packages`, and the nine-column `package|<snap\|flatpak>|<id>|<version or ->|<kind>|<revision or ->|<arch or ->|<branch or ->|<active\|inactive\|unknown>` for `store_packages`. A genuinely absent manager, prefix or store is `supported` with zero data rows; an unreadable location is `constrained` with a token, never an empty success. `root_path` is the logical path (`/opt/homebrew`, `/usr/local`, `/etc/apt`, `/var/lib/snapd`, `/var/lib/flatpak`), never an injected test root; a manager row's `version` is always `-` in this release (no `brew --version` or `dpkg --version` is run), while a Homebrew package row's `version` is the real version directory name. A snap row carries the `snap.yaml` `version` (or `-`), the `type` as a closed kind token (`app`, `gadget`, `kernel`, `base`, `snapd`, `os`; `other` for anything else, `unknown` when `snap.yaml` could not be read) and the revision; a flatpak row carries the ref id, kind `app` or `runtime`, the commit as its revision, the architecture and the branch, and always a `-` version (the branch is a ref, not a version, and `metadata` is not read). Linux never reports a manager as `unavailable`: presence is the binary, and a fact whose source could not be read is omitted with its token. A formula or cask present under both Homebrew prefixes yields one `package|` row per prefix; the package row carries no prefix column — the manager rows say which prefixes exist. Every OS-supplied field goes through the shared escaper `yuzu::util::safe_output_field`; directory names that are dot-prefixed, over 255 bytes, or contain a pipe, backslash, control or non-ASCII character are skipped without a token (Homebrew and flatpak never create them), so they never reach a row. This plugin is not in the server's `kKeyValuePlugins` set, so the server does not decode its rows as two-cell `key|rest`; the columns below are the definition's own.

privileges.measured: Not measured — the leg emits only a status row (caveat 5)

result_status.when: The read completed: managers, packages or store packages were found, or none were (an absent manager, prefix or store is a complete answer, not a degradation). A per-item degradation (below) is also `OK`.

At least one location could not be read completely, so the LIST may be incomplete. `<os>` is `macos` or `linux`; `<source>` names the location (`homebrew_taps`, `homebrew_cellar`, `homebrew_caskroom`; Linux `tool_dir`, `<tool>_bin`, `apt_sources_d`, `snapd_snaps`, `flatpak_app`, `flatpak_runtime`, and `store_packages` for the row caps); `<detail>` is `permission_denied`, `not_a_directory` (also what a symlink reads as: the kernel answers ENOTDIR to a no-follow directory open of a link), `symlink_refused` (a symlink loop in the path), `io_error`, `entry_cap` (4,096 names per directory) or `enumeration_error` (directory listing truncated or errored: its count fact is omitted, never reported as a lower bound), `row_cap` (20,000 rows), `byte_cap` (1 MiB of rows) or `walk_budget` (200,000 entries or 10 s per action; the locations not yet read are skipped and the rows already found are kept). The wall clock is cooperative: it is checked per directory and per listed entry and cannot interrupt a filesystem call that blocks on a stalled mount inside the tree (a very large listing of non-directory entries can overshoot it by the cost of its stat calls), so `<os>:<source>:busy` (source is the action name) means another dispatch of this action is still walking: nothing was read, there are no rows, retry later (at most one walk per action runs at a time). A symlinked Homebrew prefix, marker directory or store directory is refused, never followed. Several tokens are comma-joined.

**Per-item degradation is not a constraint.** On Linux `store_packages`, a single snap or flatpak whose own fields cannot be read is still emitted: an unreadable, oversized, symlinked or non-regular `snap.yaml`, a missing or unmounted revision, a `version:` that is not a plain one-line scalar passing snapd's version grammar, a broken `current` or `active` link, or an absent or unopenable `/snap` mount directory give version `-`, kind `unknown` or state `unknown` or `inactive` on the data row, and no token. The status stays `supported` because the list is complete, and the installed-software collector fails any constrained `store_packages` answer (a partial roster would delete stored rows), so a persistent per-item anomaly must never constrain the action. `linux:*` tokens therefore mean list incompleteness only.
Linux `packages`: unsupported by design; `installed_apps.list_inventory` owns the Linux package roster.
macOS `store_packages`: unsupported by design; `installed_apps` owns the macOS application list.
Windows, any action: the leg reads nothing and emits only `status|<action>|unsupported|windows:planned` (caveat 5).

Any action, any OS: a leg threw during a read. `execute()` catches it, writes `status|<action>|constrained|pkg_inventory:exception` (the one row whose level is `constrained` while the typed status is UNAVAILABLE: the command failed, rc 1) with this fixed token, never the exception's own text, and never lets the exception cross the plugin ABI.

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result AND daily-sync inventory.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore, queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`. The three actions are gathered definitions (`crossplatform.software.package_managers`, `crossplatform.software.package_manager_packages` and `crossplatform.software.store_packages`, 300s TTL).

**Also consumed by** the `installed_software` daily-sync source (`agents/core/src/sync_source_installed_software.cpp`), which calls all three actions in-process on the agent's 24 h schedule: `packages` rows become `pkg` (formula) / `app` (cask) rows with ecosystem `brew`; `managers` becomes one `homebrew` presence row (every other manager name, including the Linux ones, is read but not mapped); `store_packages` maps ACTIVE rows only, to ecosystem `snap` (kind `app` when the snap type is app, else `pkg`; version from `snap.yaml`; release = the revision) and ecosystem `flatpak` (kind `app` for apps, `pkg` for runtimes; version EMPTY because the branch is a ref and not a version; release = the commit; arch). An inactive or unknown revision is on the wire but is not installed software and never reaches the catalogue. A constrained `managers` answer keeps the cycle iff at least one PRESENT manager row was seen, mapped or not; a constrained `packages` or `store_packages` answer skips the cycle. Not consumed by TAR, DEX, or metrics.

**Sensitivity.** Rows name installed software (Homebrew formula and cask names and versions, snap and flatpak ids, versions, revisions and commits) and the package managers and Homebrew prefixes present on the host with their counts — a software inventory by another route. No row carries a username, account name or user-profile path.

**Siblings:** `installed_apps` (owns the Linux distro-package roster and the macOS application list, and its `list_per_user` also lists Homebrew formulae per user — see caveat 4 for both overlaps) and `software_actions` (installs and removes software; this plugin only reads).
